tour.title: What ClickTrail Solves
tour.description: ClickTrail is a WordPress plugin that keeps attribution data alive from ad click to conversion: through cached pages, dynamic forms, cross-domain journeys, and consent requirements. The README frames its four pillars: Capture (UTMs, click IDs, first/last-touch), WooCommerce order attribution, Form integrations, and optional server-side Delivery to ad platforms. The rest of this tour follows those same four pillars through the actual code, starting from how the plugin boots inside WordPress.

tour.title: Plugin Bootstrap
tour.description: clicutcl.php is the WordPress plugin header file: it defines core constants, registers activation/deactivation hooks, and initializes the plugin on WordPress's init hook. Before anything else runs, it loads class-autoloader.php, which maps CLICUTCL_-prefixed and namespaced class names to file paths under includes/ via spl_autoload_register. This pair is the plugin's front door -- every other class in this tour becomes reachable only because the autoloader wires it up.
tour.languageLesson: WordPress plugins have no bundler or module system, so PHP autoloading (spl_autoload_register) is the mechanism that turns a naming convention (class-consent-mode.php -> Consent_Mode) into on-demand file loading, replacing dozens of manual require_once calls.

tour.title: The Core Orchestrator
tour.description: includes/class-clicutcl-core.php is the central orchestrator: it boots admin and public hooks, builds the JS-facing configuration objects (consent bridge, attribution, WooCommerce data layer), and enqueues the front-end tracking script. It relies on two small but widely-used foundations: class-context.php, a value object exposing the plugin's directory path, URL, and basename, and class-setting.php, the base class that models every WordPress option the plugin manages. Nearly every module explained later in this tour extends or calls into these two classes.

tour.title: Capturing Events: The Tracking Controller
tour.description: includes/api/class-tracking-controller.php registers the plugin's REST API routes for batch event ingestion, attribution-token signing/verification, webhook intake, order lifecycle updates, and delivery diagnostics -- this is the server-side landing point for everything the browser captures. Legacy payloads arrive in an older shape, so class-event-translator-v1-to-v2.php translates V1 tracking events into the canonical V2 event schema, inferring funnel stage and intent along the way. Together they implement the README's promise that no click ID or UTM disappears after the landing page.

tour.title: Consent-Aware Gating
tour.description: ClickTrail's core design constraint is consent-aware capture with no external identification calls. class-consent-mode-settings.php models Google Consent Mode configuration (mode, target regions, CMP source, GCM keys) and resolves whether a given request's geolocation requires consent -- it has the highest fan-in of any settings class in the codebase, meaning nearly every capture and delivery path checks it before acting. class-consent-mode.php uses those settings to register Consent Mode's default consent state and render the gtag consentDefault snippet before GTM loads.

tour.title: GTM Tag Rendering
tour.description: Once consent state is resolved, class-gtm-settings.php models the Google Tag Manager configuration (container ID, delivery mode, tagging server URL) and builds sanitized script/noscript tag URLs, while class-web-tag.php actually renders the GTM script tag in the page head and the noscript iframe fallback in the body. This is the mechanism through which ClickTrail's captured attribution data reaches Google's tag ecosystem in the browser, gated by the consent settings from Step 5.

tour.title: The Browser-Side Capture Engine
tour.description: The PHP classes so far configure and gate; this JavaScript quartet does the actual capturing in the visitor's browser. clicutcl-attribution.js captures UTMs, click IDs, and referrer data, buffering them pre-consent in sessionStorage and persisting to cookies once consent is granted. clicutcl-consent-bridge.js normalizes consent signals from multiple sources (ClickTrail's own banner, Cookiebot, OneTrust, Complianz, Google Consent Mode) into one signal the rest of the JS relies on, fed by clicutcl-consent.js's native consent banner. clicutcl-events.js then batches browser events (scroll depth, downloads, WooCommerce interactions) for transport to the Tracking Controller from Step 4.
tour.languageLesson: This module uses a bridge pattern in plain JS: rather than every script special-casing which consent platform is installed, clicutcl-consent-bridge.js normalizes all of them behind one interface, so downstream code (attribution, events) only ever reads a single normalized signal.

tour.title: Form Integrations
tour.description: The README promises hidden-field enrichment for forms even on cached or dynamic pages. interface-form-adapter.php defines the contract every third-party form adapter must implement, and class-abstract-form-adapter.php provides the shared base -- identity extraction, attribution logging, payload anonymization -- that concrete adapters like class-cf7-adapter.php (Contact Form 7) build on. class-form-integration-manager.php ties it together at runtime, detecting which form plugins are active and activating only the matching adapters, an interface-driven plugin-within-a-plugin pattern.
tour.languageLesson: PHP interfaces plus an abstract base class form a two-layer contract here: the interface guarantees a minimal method set for any adapter, while the abstract class adds shared implementation (identity extraction, anonymization) so concrete adapters like the CF7 one only implement what's genuinely form-specific.

tour.title: Server-Side Delivery
tour.description: class-adapter-interface.php has the highest fan-in of any file in the codebase: it defines the contract every server-side delivery adapter (Meta, Google Ads, TikTok, and others) must implement to send events and report health. class-dispatcher.php is the central dispatcher that builds the configured adapter, checks consent one more time, sends events, and records health/failure telemetry for the admin diagnostics dashboard. This is the optional last step in the README's pipeline: consent-aware, server-to-server delivery to ad platforms.

tour.title: Admin UI and Setup
tour.description: class-admin.php is the plugin's central WordPress admin controller: it registers menus, settings, and assets, and handles saving and sanitizing every settings group covered so far (attribution, consent mode, GTM, server-side delivery, tracking v2). class-setup-wizard.php is the multi-step onboarding screen that walks a new site owner through configuration, using environment detection to pre-fill recommended settings -- the human-facing counterpart to all the Setting subclasses from Steps 3, 5, and 6.

tour.title: Lifecycle, Storage, and Privacy
tour.description: class-installer.php handles activation-time database setup, creating and upgrading ClickTrail's custom tables via dbDelta. class-privacy-handler.php implements WordPress's personal-data export/erase hooks for GDPR compliance, scrubbing captured attribution events tied to a user's email or ID. uninstall.php is the mirror image of clicutcl.php from Step 2: on removal, it deletes options, clears scheduled jobs, and drops the custom tables the installer created, closing the plugin's lifecycle loop.

tour.title: Tests and Continuous Integration
tour.description: BoundarySecurityTest.php is a PHPUnit regression suite covering exactly the security-sensitive boundaries this tour has walked through: server-only event gating, consent cookie resolution, PII redaction of retry payloads, and webhook signature verification. The phpunit.yml GitHub Actions workflow runs that suite across a matrix of PHP 8.1, 8.2, and 8.3 on every push and pull request, making sure the consent and delivery guarantees from Steps 5-9 don't silently regress.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions matrix builds (php-version: [8.1, 8.2, 8.3]) run the same job definition once per matrix value in parallel, catching version-specific regressions without duplicating workflow YAML.

tour.title: Project Map and Configuration
tour.description: docs/architecture/CODE-MAP.md is the canonical map of the plugin's active file layout, cross-referencing the root files, docs/, and includes/ tree this tour has traced end to end. composer.json declares the PHP 8.1+ requirement, the PSR-4 autoload mapping (CLICUTCL\ to includes/) that underpins Step 2's autoloader, and the dev tooling (PHPCS/WPCS, PHPUnit) exercised by Step 12's CI. Together they're the reference to return to once you've internalized how capture, consent, delivery, and admin fit together.
